title: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn
desc: Historia de EE.UU. desde abajo: esclavos, obreros, mujeres, indígenas. Desmonta el mito del excepcionalismo americano.
tesis: La historia de Estados Unidos no es la historia de sus presidentes, generales y capitalistas — es la historia de la gente que resistió, luchó y fue silenciada. Zinn reescribe la historia norteamericana desde la perspectiva de los indígenas masacrados, los esclavos africanos, las obreras textiles, los socialistas perseguidos y los movimientos sociales que el relato oficial borra o domestica. Colón no fue un explorador valiente sino el iniciador de un genocidio. La Constitución no fue un pacto democrático sino un acuerdo entre propietarios blancos. Cada guerra fue vendida con propaganda patriótica mientras servía intereses económicos. El 'sueño americano' es un mito funcional para mantener a los oprimidos esperando en lugar de organizándose.
ideas: La historia la escriben los vencedores: la memoria del Estado no es nuestra memoria. Aceptarla acríticamente es aceptar la perspectiva de los conquistadores.
El genocidio indígena no fue un 'efecto colateral' de la colonización sino su método principal: de 10 millones de nativos a menos de un millón.
La Constitución de EE.UU. fue diseñada por y para propietarios blancos. Los 'Padres Fundadores' temían más a la democracia popular que a la tiranía.
Cada guerra estadounidense — 1812, México, España, Primera y Segunda Mundial, Corea, Vietnam, Irak — fue impulsada por intereses económicos y vendida con propaganda patriótica.
Los derechos no se otorgan desde arriba — se conquistan desde abajo: abolición, sufragio femenino, derechos civiles, derechos laborales. Todos costaron sangre.
contexto: Publicado en 1980 y convertido en bestseller con más de 2 millones de copias vendidas. Zinn (1922-2010), veterano de la Segunda Guerra Mundial y activista de derechos civiles, escribió la historia de Estados Unidos que los libros de texto no cuentan: la de los trabajadores, esclavos, mujeres, indígenas y disidentes.
porqueLeer: Porque desmonta el excepcionalismo americano pieza por pieza, con documentación rigurosa y prosa accesible. Es el antídoto perfecto contra la propaganda que presenta a EE.UU. como faro de democracia y libertad. Para cualquier latinoamericano, es esencial entender cómo el imperio se ve a sí mismo — y cómo lo ven sus propios disidentes.

conexiones.razon: Parenti analiza el imperio contemporáneo; Zinn traza su historia desde Colón hasta Vietnam.
Galeano cuenta la historia desde las víctimas latinoamericanas; Zinn desde las víctimas dentro de EE.UU.
Lenin teorizó el imperialismo; Zinn documenta su aplicación práctica por Estados Unidos.
Ambos reescriben la historia oficial de sus países desde los pueblos negados: indígenas, negros, obreros.

quotes.text: To emphasize the heroism of Columbus and his successors as navigators and discoverers, and to deemphasize their genocide, is not a technical necessity but an ideological choice. It serves — unwittingly — to justify what was done.

The historian's distortion is more than technical, it is ideological; it is released into a world of contending interests, where any chosen emphasis supports (whether the historian means to or not) some kind of interest, whether economic or political or racial or national or sexual.

My viewpoint, in telling the history of the United States, is different: that we must not accept the memory of states as our own. Nations are not communities and never have been. The history of any country, presented as the history of a family, conceals fierce conflicts of interest between conquerors and conquered, masters and slaves, capitalists and workers, dominators and dominated in race and sex.

tl: Colon descubre America y rehabilita la esclavitud

They were well-built, with good bodies and handsome features. They do not bear arms, and do not know them, for I showed them a sword, they took it by the edge and cut themselves. They would make fine servants. With fifty men we could subjugate them all and make them do whatever we want.
Rebelion de Bacon sacude la Virginia colonial

In 1676, seventy years after Virginia was founded, a hundred years before it supplied leadership for the American Revolution, that colony faced a rebellion of white frontiersmen, joined by slaves and servants, a rebellion so threatening that the governor had to flee the burning capital of Jamestown.
Rebelion de esclavos en Stono, Carolina del Sur

At Stono, South Carolina, in 1739, about twenty slaves rebelled, killed two warehouse guards, stole guns and gunpowder, and headed south, killing people in their way, and burning buildings. They were joined by others, until there were perhaps eighty slaves in all.
Masacre de Boston: trabajadores contra soldados britanicos

On March 5, 1770, grievances of ropemakers against British soldiers taking their jobs led to a fight. A crowd gathered in front of the customhouse and began provoking the soldiers, who fired and killed first Crispus Attucks, a mulatto worker, then others.
Declaración de Independencia de Filadelfia

The Declaration of Independence brought that myth to its peak of eloquence. Each of the developments of the previous decade, the Proclamation of 1763 not allowing whites to settle beyond the Appalachians, the Stamp Tax, the Townshend taxes, the stationing of troops and the Boston Massacre.
Rebelion de Nat Turner en Virginia

Nat Turner's rebellion in Southampton County, Virginia, in the summer of 1831, threw the slaveholding South into a panic, and then into a determined effort to bolster the security of the slave system. Turner, claiming religious visions, gathered about seventy slaves.
Sendero de las Lagrimas: deportacion cherokee

But the seventeen thousand Cherokees were soon rounded up and crowded into stockades. On October 1, 1838, the first detachment set out in what was to be known as the Trail of Tears. As they moved westward, they began to die of sickness, of drought, of the heat, of exposure.
Lincoln es electo y el Sur inicia la secesión

So, when Lincoln was elected, seven southern states seceded from the Union. Lincoln initiated hostilities by trying to repossess the federal base at Fort Sumter, South Carolina, and four more states seceded. The Confederacy was formed; the Civil War was on.
Proclamacion de Emancipacion: limitada y militar

Thus, when the Emancipation Proclamation was issued January 1, 1863, it declared slaves free in those areas still fighting against the Union (which it listed very carefully), and said nothing about slaves behind Union lines. As Hofstadter put it, the Emancipation Proclamation had all the moral grandeur of a bill of lading.
Haymarket: bomba, juicio amanado, anarquistas colgados

With no evidence on who threw the bomb, the police arrested eight anarchist leaders in Chicago. The Chicago Journal said: Justice should be prompt in dealing with the arrested anarchists. The law regarding accessories to crime in this State is so plain that their trials will be short.
Masacre de Wounded Knee: cierre de la frontera con sangre

The black was being kept under control in the South. The Indian was being driven off the western plains for good; on a cold winter day in 1890, U.S. army soldiers attacked Indians camped at Wounded Knee, South Dakota, and killed three hundred men, women, and children.
Huelga de Pullman: el sindicato contra el monopolio ferroviario

In June 1894, workers at the Pullman Palace Car Company went on strike. We struck at Pullman because we were without hope. We joined the American Railway Union because it gave us a glimmer of hope. Twenty thousand souls, men, women and little ones, have their eyes turned toward this convention today.
Incendio en Triangle Shirtwaist mata a 146 obreras

On the afternoon of March 25, 1911, a fire at the Triangle Shirtwaist Company that began in a rag bin swept through the eighth, ninth, and tenth floors, too high for fire ladders to reach. But at the Triangle Company the doors opened in. The law said the doors could not be locked.
Huelga textil de Lawrence dirigida por la IWW

The IWW became involved in a set of dramatic events in Lawrence, Massachusetts, in the year 1912, where the American Woolen Company owned four mills. A considerable number of the boys and girls die within the first two or three years after beginning work.
Ley de Espionaje aplasta disidencia antibelica

The Espionage Act was used to imprison Americans who spoke or wrote against the war. Eugene Debs was arrested for violating the Espionage Act. There were a thousand people prosecuted under the Espionage Act and the Sedition Act, for opposing the war.
Ejecucion de Sacco y Vanzetti

The trial record and the surrounding circumstances suggested that Sacco and Vanzetti were sentenced to death because they were anarchists and foreigners. In August 1927, as police broke up marches and picket lines with arrests and beatings, and troops surrounded the prison, they were electrocuted.
Ejercito de los Bonos marcha sobre Washington

The anger of the veteran of the First World War, now without work, his family hungry, led to the march of the Bonus Army to Washington in the spring and summer of 1932. War veterans, holding government bonus certificates which were due years in the future, demanded that Congress pay off on them now.
Huelga de brazos caidos en Flint, victoria contra GM

In December of that year began the longest sit-down strike of all, at Fisher Body plant #1 in Flint, Michigan. It started when two brothers were fired, and it lasted until February 1937. For forty days there was a community of two thousand strikers.
Hiroshima y Nagasaki: la bomba atomica como mensaje

On August 6, 1945, came the lone American plane in the sky over Hiroshima, dropping the first atomic bomb, leaving perhaps 100,000 Japanese dead, and tens of thousands more slowly dying from radiation poisoning. Three days later, a second atomic bomb was dropped on the city of Nagasaki.
McCarthy y la cacera de brujas anticomunista

Senator Joseph McCarthy of Wisconsin could go even further than Truman. Speaking to a Women's Republican Club in Wheeling, West Virginia, in early 1950, he held up some papers and shouted: I have here in my hand a list of 205 names that were made known to the Secretary of State as being members of the Communist Party.
Brown v. Board: la Corte tumba 'separados pero iguales'

In 1954, the Court finally struck down the separate but equal doctrine that it had defended since the 1890s. The NAACP brought a series of cases before the Court to challenge segregation in the public schools, and now in Brown v. Board of Education the Court said the separation of schoolchildren generates a feeling of inferiority.
Sentadas de Greensboro encienden el movimiento estudiantil

On February 1, 1960, four freshmen at a Negro college in Greensboro, North Carolina, decided to sit down at the Woolworth's lunch counter downtown, where only whites ate. They were refused service, and when they would not leave, the lunch counter was closed for the day.
Marcha sobre Washington: 'Tengo un sueño'

When black civil rights leaders planned a huge march on Washington in the summer of 1963 to protest the failure of the nation to solve the race problem, it was quickly embraced by President Kennedy and other national leaders, and turned into a friendly assemblage.
Masacre de My Lai en Vietnam del Sur

On March 16, 1968, a company of American soldiers went into the hamlet of My Lai 4, in Quang Ngai province. They rounded up the inhabitants, including old people and women with infants in their arms. These people were ordered into a ditch, where they were methodically shot to death by American soldiers.
Asesinato de Martin Luther King en Memphis

He went to Memphis, Tennessee, to support a strike of garbage workers in that city. There, standing on a balcony outside his hotel room, he was shot to death by an unseen marksman. As a Senate report on the FBI said in 1976, the FBI tried to destroy Dr. Martin Luther King.
Masacre estudiantil de Kent State

The climax of protest came in the spring of 1970 when President Nixon ordered the invasion of Cambodia. At Kent State University in Ohio, on May 4, when students gathered to demonstrate against the war, National Guardsmen fired into the crowd. Four students were killed.
Filtracion de los Papeles del Pentagono

In September of 1971, shortly after the New York Times printed Daniel Ellsberg's copies of the top-secret Pentagon Papers, the administration planned and carried out, Howard Hunt and Gordon Liddy themselves doing it, the burglary of the office of Ellsberg's psychiatrist, looking for Ellsberg's records.
COINTELPRO: el FBI contra los Panteras Negras y la izquierda

Between 1956 and 1971 the FBI conducted a massive Counterintelligence Program (known as COINTELPRO) that took 295 actions against black groups. A secret FBI report to President Nixon in 1970 said a recent poll indicates that approximately 25% of the black population has a great respect for the Black Panther Party.
AIM ocupa Wounded Knee de nuevo

On February 27, 1973, about three hundred Oglala Sioux, many of them members of the new militant organization called the American Indian Movement (AIM), entered the village of Wounded Knee and declared it liberated territory.
Watergate: renuncia historica de Nixon

On top of this came the political disgrace of the Nixon administration in the scandals that came to be known by the one-word label Watergate, and which led to the historic resignation from the presidency, the first in American history, of Richard Nixon in August 1974.
